-- The TARGET is these definitions, which also appear in the context: d14
def d14 (N : S1 X Y) (T : ℕ) : S1 X Y where
  A1 := Fin T × N.A1
  a2 := inferInstance
  A3 := fun a => N.A3 a.2
  a4 := fun a => N.a4 a.2
  a5 := fun a σ x =>
    N.a5 a.2 (fun m => if h : a.1.val = 0 then N.a4 m else σ (⟨a.1.val - 1, by omega⟩, m)) x
  a6 := fun σ =>
    if h : T = 0 then N.a6 N.a4 else N.a6 (fun m => σ (⟨T - 1, by omega⟩, m))
a_raw: {"translation":"For arbitrary types X and Y, d14 takes a record N of type S1 X Y and then a natural number T, and constructs another record of type S1 X Y. Its indices are all pairs (i, n) with 0 ≤ i < T and n an index of N. This index type is finite because both factors are finite. At each (i, n), the state type is N.A3 n and the initial value is N.a4 n. To update (i, n) from a full current state σ and input x, apply N.a5 at n with input x and the following assignment of states to the indices of N: if i = 0, give every m its initial value N.a4 m, ignoring σ; if i > 0, give every m the value σ(i − 1, m) from the preceding layer. The output from σ is N.a6 applied to the initial assignment N.a4 if T = 0 (when there are no indices), and otherwise is N.a6 applied to the assignment m ↦ σ(T − 1, m) from the last layer. No additional hypothesis on N or T is required; this defines the record rather than asserting a property of it."}

divergences.description: The construction accepts any network in the finite-node, synchronous `S1` model; it does not require the original network to be recurrent.
`T` fixes the number of copies, not a limit on execution. The pipeline can keep updating after step `T`, without any assertion that those later outputs match the original’s.
At `T = 0` there is no last copy. Lean returns the original network’s initial output, `N.a6 N.a4`, a convention not specified in the passages.

judgement.summary: For positive `T`, the definition matches the declared pipeline variant rather than the passages’ once-per-copy schedule. Every copy starts in the original initial state and updates on each current input; the first always reads that initial state, each later copy reads its predecessor’s pre-update state, and the readout uses the last copy.
